Yes. The data indicate **0.7 hectares of tree-cover loss in 2023**, about 1.2% of the 58.1-hectare property. The entire loss area was mapped as forest in 2020.

Uruguay’s 2021 forest map classified 0.4 hectares of the loss area as planted eucalyptus and 0.3 hectares as outside mapped forest; none was mapped as native forest. An additional 0.4 hectares of loss occurred in smaller patches that did not meet the tool’s event-size threshold.

Tree-cover loss does not by itself establish the cause or whether the land was permanently cleared.
